cli_result.result:
Validation passed (exit 0). Evaluation complete.

**Definition check — the sentence from "Source rubric and schema paths (#158)", verbatim and in full:**

> Read release-specific notes from the dedicated `updates.update_details` field, `updates.description` or `notes`, requiring actual release or derivation information rather than crediting unrelated notes.

The section is present and reads as expected of the current rules (it names the dedicated `updates.update_details` slot and the anti-crediting requirement), so I proceeded.

**Result: 49/50 — fixed 98.0% (÷50), normalized 98.0% (÷50), 0 sub-elements N/A.**

Applicability resolved from other elements' evidence before scoring: datasets-shared met (`distribution_formats`, public FAIRhub access route, reuse-permitting license); human subjects met (E1 `description` "2,280 adults…in-person study visit", E8 `collection_mechanisms`/`direct_collection` recruitment); data collection met; the software-output gate for E8.3 met only borderline via the `https://github.com/AI-READI` organization root, so the ambiguity rule applied (applicable, scored). Nothing was excluded, so both denominators are 50.

The single lost point is **E8 sub-element 4 (Software and Tools)**. The record describes the conversions that created the distributed files (`.fda`/`.sdt` → DICOM, `.FIT` → Open mHealth, OMOP ETL, "automated and custom processing") but never names the tools. Every named piece of software sits in an excluded role: REDCap and MoCA Duo are capture (a), FAIRhub is hosting (b), RO-Crate is packaging (c), the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard is validation (d). The GitHub pointer identifies the publisher, not a tool, so it neither earns nor forfeits the point.

Three consistency checks failed and eight warnings were raised — notably `confidentiality_level: restricted`, which the record itself states contradicts the only sourced value (HL7:2N normal), and three incompatible deidentification characterizations (NoDeIdentification / `deidentified: true` / Safe Harbor). Both are disclosed by the record rather than concealed, which is why they cost points nowhere but are logged. Twenty checks passed, including full arithmetic reconciliation of the cohort (all demographic breakdowns and all three splits total 2,280, with per-group sums across splits matching) and of the file counts (nine collections sum to nine files short of `total_file_count`, exactly the root metadata files).

One disclosure: in E2 sub-element 3 the evidence string contains a typographic garble, `third_party_sharing.is_sharedttrue`, where `is_shared: true` was intended. The record's value and the adjacent quotation are accurate; I left it rather than regenerate the whole artifact from context for a cosmetic defect, since a full re-emit risks silent divergence in other fields. Post-write edits were unavailable — the sandbox denied every Bash path that writes.

Output is at `output_evaluation.json`, validated with the exact command requested.
